record.narrative:
All estimates and intervals below are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For outcome_006, I use an operational clinically meaningful absolute-scale threshold of about 0.0175, approximately 10% of the absolute mean outcome scale. H285 through H288 test whether the accepted feature_021 association with outcome_006 persists in additional strata. Their signed estimates are very large and positive: H285 +0.393 in feature_065=1; H286 +0.397 in feature_065=0; H287 +0.477 in high feature_043; and H288 +0.315 in low feature_043. Every signed lower bound is far above the outcome_006 support threshold, and all comparison cells meet the minimum-size rule. I accept these as dataset-specific confirmations/localizations of the dominant feature_021=1 versus feature_021=0 association with weaker outcome_006 dependency. They are not independent causal predictors, and H287/H288 should not be read as evidence for feature_043 effect modification because the separate feature_043 interaction line failed independent validation.

H289 tested the prespecified positive interaction between feature_021 and high versus complement of median feature_010 for outcome_006. The signed estimate is large and negative, -0.789, with a signed 95% interval entirely negative from -0.904 to -0.674. That is the opposite of the claimed positive direction and below the support threshold, so I reject H289 and close that positive-interaction claim. The magnitude is surprising enough that it may indicate opposite effect modification or some sensitivity to the median split; however, no independent validation can be requested, and this is one of many secondary interaction screens. I therefore do not automatically accept the opposite interaction. I registered the two simple mean-difference contrasts in the feature_010 strata and a reversed-direction interaction proposal only to determine whether the negative interaction reflects a coherent reversed simple effect or an unstable median-split artifact.

H290 is a near-null feature_015 interaction: signed estimate +0.001, interval -0.141 to +0.144. It does not support clinically meaningful positive effect modification, so I reject and close it. H291 through H293 test residual secondary categorical contrasts with outcome_006 restricted to feature_021=0. H291 has a negative signed point estimate, H292 has a positive point estimate below threshold although its upper bound crosses threshold, and H293 has a negative signed point estimate within the no-support range. Given multiplicity, lack of independent validation capacity, and the need for a clear estimate and lower bound above threshold for secondary claims, I reject these residual associations and close them. No leakage is apparent: exposures, predictors, stratifiers, and outcomes are distinct measured variables, and all cells are valid. All conclusions remain associations in this supplied dataset rather than causal or generalizable biology. I did not request validation because remaining new validation requests are exhausted.

Iteration 21/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: Final report for this supplied dataset. The dominant supported finding remains that feature_021=1 versus feature_021=0 is associated with much weaker outcome_006 dependency, because more negative scores indicate stronger dependency and the accepted signed contrasts are positive. Discovery R121 estimated +0.396 (95% interval +0.325 to +0.467), and independent validation R127 estimated +0.435 with an adjusted interval +0.334 to +0.536; both are far above the operational 10% absolute-scale benchmark for outcome_006. Accepted subgroup mean differences for feature_021 should be interpreted as dataset-specific localization or concordance of this same association, not as independent causal predictors. H272 is reassessed because validation response R235 is due. H272 proposed a positive feature_043-median interaction for the feature_021-outcome_006 association. Discovery R233 was positive and threshold-proximal (+0.162, lower bound +0.021), but independent validation R235 gave a negative point estimate of -0.059 with adjusted interval -0.262 to +0.144. The validation point estimate is opposite the claimed direction, the adjusted lower bound is far below the operational outcome_006 interaction support threshold, and the interval is compatible with no clinically meaningful positive interaction. Therefore H272 remains rejected and closed; the feature_043 interaction claim is not supported. Other released validations also failed: H261 feature_057 positive interaction and H279 residual feature_065-outcome_015 association were not replicated by independent validation. The principal unresolved secondary question is the feature_010 median interaction line. The original positive interaction H289 was rejected because the signed discovery evidence was strongly negative. The reversed interaction H296 has a very large positive signed discovery estimate (+0.789, interval +0.674 to +0.904), but it is a post hoc reversal of the original sign and lacks independent validation. It is therefore treated as unresolved active pending the already registered simple feature_010 stratum contrasts H294 and H295. The most informative next analysis is not broad subgroup mining: complete the feature_010 simple strata to determine whether high feature_010 attenuates or abolishes the main feature_021-outcome_006 association, and perform model-based robustness or adjustment analyses for the main feature_021-outcome_006 association. All accepted conclusions remain associations in this supplied dataset, not causal effects or externally generalizable biology.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: All displayed estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For outcome_006 I treat approximately 0.0175 as the operational absolute-scale benchmark associated with a 10% relative difference. H295 and H298 are simple feature_021=1 versus feature_021=0 contrasts in low-feature_010 strata. Their signed estimates are +0.810 and +0.808 with lower bounds +0.781 and +0.768, respectively, far beyond the benchmark and with valid cells. I accept these as dataset-specific localization of the main association: in low-feature_010 subsets, feature_021=1 is associated with a much less negative outcome_006 score, i.e. weaker dependency, than feature_021=0. H300 and H301 similarly provide strong signed support for a feature_010 gradient: H300 is +0.548 with lower bound +0.451, supporting enhancement of the feature_021 contrast in the low quartile relative to its complement, while H301 is +0.457 with lower bound +0.286, supporting attenuation or reversal in the high quartile relative to its complement. H296, the reversed median-interaction claim, is also strongly supported on its own registered direction (+0.789, lower bound +0.674) and, crucially, is coherent with the simple low/median and quartile tests. I therefore accept H296 only as a dataset-specific association pattern: the feature_021--outcome_006 association is strongly present when feature_010 is low and strongly attenuated when feature_010 is high. This is not evidence of a reversed simple main effect within the high stratum, nor a causal effect-modification conclusion. H294 is small positive (+0.021) with a wide interval and does not meet the acceptability threshold; it is therefore left unresolved rather than accepted. H297 and H299 test reversed simple effects in high-feature_010 strata; both have negative signed point estimates (-0.021 and -0.062) and are not supported, but their intervals are wide enough that I record them as inconclusive/unresolved rather than proving absence of any high-stratum reversal. No leakage is apparent: feature_021, feature_010, and outcome_006 are distinct measured variables, and all cells are valid. The main limitation is multiplicity and the fact that H296 was proposed as a reversed interaction after rejecting H289; however, the newly registered low/high simple contrasts and quartile interactions form a coherent pattern. Independent validation is no longer available, so this remains an association in the supplied dataset only, not a causal or externally generalizable claim. record.narrative: Final synthesis for the supplied dataset, including the due validation response for H279. H279 tested whether, among cells with feature_021=0 and feature_060=0, feature_065=1 versus 0 was associated with a more negative outcome_015 score, i.e. stronger dependency, in the registered negative direction. The discovery Welch result R241 was positive and nominally significant: signed estimate +0.0409, 95% interval +0.0111 to +0.0708. The lower bound is modest, near the 10% absolute-scale benchmark for an outcome_015 mean around -0.25, so the discovery evidence was already not robustly clinically meaningful. The independent validation response R247 reversed the sign and was not significant: signed estimate -0.0036, adjusted interval -0.0507 to +0.0435. This does not replicate the discovery residual association and is compatible with no clinically meaningful effect. Therefore H279 is rejected and closed: there is no supported residual feature_065 association with outcome_015 in this residual feature_021/feature_060 stratum. More broadly, the final evidence pattern is that most measured predictors and simple subgroup comparisons have null or insufficiently supported effects, while one strong validated line stands out. The main supported association is outcome_006 feature_021=1 versus feature_021=0. Because outcome scores are dependency measures and more negative values mean stronger dependency, the positive signed mean_difference indicates weaker dependency in feature_021=1 relative to feature_021=0. The overall discovery estimate was +0.396, 95% interval +0.325 to +0.467, and independent validation was +0.435, adjusted interval +0.334 to +0.536. These effects are far above the outcome_006 operational absolute benchmark of roughly 0.0175 and are therefore scientifically meaningful in this dataset as an association. Accepted feature_010 effect-modification results refine the localization of this main association, not add a separate validated predictor. The accepted signed interaction line H296, together with low-feature_010 simple contrasts and quartile interactions, supports the dataset-specific pattern that the feature_021 association with outcome_006 is very strong when feature_010 is low and strongly attenuated when feature_010 is high. This is effect modification or localization in this supplied dataset only; it does not establish that feature_010 causally modifies the association, nor that the magnitude will generalize. The main feature_021 outcome_006 finding itself has independent validation, but still supports association rather than causality. Negative or unsupported findings are important for narrowing conclusions. The original feature_043 median-interaction claim H272 is not supported after independent validation: discovery suggested a positive interaction but validation R235 had the opposite sign and an adjusted interval spanning no meaningful effect. The feature_057 interaction H261 was also not validated. The feature_002 outcome_006 lines remain unsupported overall and in simple feature_034 strata; validation intervals are near null and do not support a clinically meaningful association. The current H279 result further shows that smaller residual associations involving feature_065 with outcome_015 or outcome_014 should not be promoted without replication. Many other deferred or closed subgroup claims remain unresolved or rejected because the point estimates are small, intervals include null, or the lower bounds do not clear the clinically meaningful threshold. Remaining uncertainty is mainly biological interpretation and external generalizability. Feature_010 modification is data-derived and post hoc, and feature_021's role is inferred from association, not causal mechanism. The most informative next analysis is not broader subgroup mining. If external data become available, pre-specify and test the main feature_021 outcome_006 association and the feature_010 low/high effect modification with multiplicity-aware methods. In the current data, the most useful follow-up would be model-based robustness analysis of the feature_021 outcome_006 association and feature_010 modification, including covariate adjustment, nonlinear quantile modeling around feature_010, measurement/assay-level checks if available, and causal-sensitivity diagnostics. Study instructions:

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

For outcome_006 I used the approximate absolute 10% benchmark of 0.0175 as the operational scale for scientific meaningfulness. Positive simple contrasts mean feature_021=1 is associated with a less negative outcome_006 dependency score than feature_021=0, i.e. weaker dependency. Positive direction -1 interaction estimates mean a raw negative interaction, i.e. attenuation or reversal of the feature_021 contrast in the named high-feature_010 subset relative to its feature_010 complement within the same feature_060 eligibility stratum. H303 and H304 provide low-feature_010 simple contrasts split by feature_060: H303 is +0.793 with lower bound +0.739 in feature_060=0, and H304 is +0.823 with lower bound +0.762 in feature_060=1. Both exclude the null and far exceed the meaningfulness benchmark, with valid cells, so I accept them as dataset-specific evidence that the feature_021 association with outcome_006 is very strong when feature_010 is low, across both feature_060 strata. H307 and H308 test the corresponding high-feature_010 attenuation interactions within feature_060=0 and feature_060=1. H307 is +0.399 with lower bound +0.148, and H308 is +0.513 with lower bound +0.274; both have clear precision beyond the benchmark. I accept them as dataset-specific evidence that the feature_021 association is much weaker in high-feature_010 cells than in their feature_010 complements within the same feature_060 stratum. H302, H305, and H306 test the raw positive residual simple association in high-feature_010 strata. Their signed estimates are positive but uncertain: H302 +0.062 with interval including null and lower bound -0.092; H305 +0.099 with lower bound -0.131; H306 +0.030 with lower bound -0.184. Because the lower bounds fall below the meaningfulness benchmark and include no effect, the residual simple high-stratum effect is not established. I leave these unresolved and close them because the accepted low-stratum simple contrasts and high-stratum interaction contrasts are the scientifically useful localization, and no validation capacity remains. Multiplicity and post hoc quantile-splitting remain limitations. No validation request is made because remaining new validation requests are zero. Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

record.narrative: No assessments are due and no new independent validation requests remain. I therefore consolidated the final dataset-specific conclusions and reassessed several validation-exposed claims that had remained unresolved because their validation responses were near null or opposite sign: H7, H30, H34, H55, and H77 are changed to reject and closed because neither discovery nor validation gives robust evidence of a difference of at least 10 percent relative to the absolute outcome scale. The strongest supported finding in the supplied dataset is an association between feature_021=1 versus feature_021=0 and outcome_006. Because dependency scores are more negative for stronger dependency, positive signed mean-differences for direction +1 mean feature_021=1 cells have less negative outcome_006 scores, i.e. weaker dependency. The overall discovery estimate was +0.396 (95 percent interval +0.325 to +0.467), and independent validation was +0.435 (adjusted interval +0.334 to +0.536). The absolute mean outcome_006 scale is about 0.175, so the 10 percent operational benchmark is roughly 0.0175; both estimates are far above this benchmark and exclude the null. This is supported as an association in this dataset, not as causality or generalizable biology. The feature_021 outcome_006 association was also seen in many accepted subgroup contrasts, but the most informative internal localization involves feature_010. Accepted low-feature_010 simple contrasts are very large, including +0.810 (+0.781 to +0.839) at the feature_010 median split and +0.793 (+0.739 to +0.847) and +0.823 (+0.762 to +0.884) within feature_060=0 and feature_060=1 strata respectively. Corresponding accepted feature_010-high attenuation interactions are also large, including +0.789 (+0.674 to +0.904) overall and +0.399 (+0.148 to +0.650) and +0.513 (+0.274 to +0.751) within feature_060=0 and feature_060=1. These results support a dataset-specific effect-modification or localization pattern: the feature_021 outcome_006 association is extremely strong when feature_010 is low and strongly attenuated when feature_010 is high. They are not independent-validated, are post hoc in the feature_010 split, and do not establish that feature_010 causally modifies the association. The residual simple high-feature_010 contrasts remain uncertain and should not be promoted. The final negative picture is broad. Most simple predictor-outcome comparisons are null, too small, or imprecise. The feature_002 outcome_006 line is not supported after validation. Several discovery-only subgroup interactions failed validation, including the feature_043 median interaction for outcome_006 and the feature_057 interaction for outcome_006. The feature_008 outcome_008 association was only nominally discoverable and did not validate. Feature_048-level associations with outcome_009 in subgroups remain unsupported as clinically meaningful effects, and the H279 residual feature_065 outcome_015 association reversed in validation. I therefore treat smaller residual subgroup findings as noise unless they form a pre-specified, coherent, and externally replicated pattern. Unresolved uncertainty remains for small effects near the 10 percent threshold, especially the raw feature_021 contrast for outcome_005, some feature_065 residual associations with outcome_014 and outcome_015, and many deferred subgroup claims. These are either below the threshold, have intervals crossing null or the threshold, or lack validation. The main limitations are opaque predictor labels, correlated predictors, multiplicity, post hoc quantile splits, and the exhaustion of independent validation capacity. The next best analysis is not further broad subgroup mining but pre-specified model-based robustness and external replication of the feature_021 outcome_006 association and its feature_010 modification, including covariate adjustment, nonlinear modeling of feature_010, assay-level checks, causal-sensitivity diagnostics, and multiplicity-aware confirmation in independent data.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and validation capacity is exhausted, so this final explore stage registers discovery-only refinements of the one strongly supported dataset-specific association: feature_021=1 versus feature_021=0 is associated with a much less negative outcome_006 score, meaning weaker CRISPR dependency. The prior evidence indicates that the association is very strong when feature_010 is low, absent or null-like in the median-to-third-quartile feature_010 band, and attenuated or weak when feature_010 is high. Those comparisons are still too coarse to decide whether the pattern is a smooth gradient, a threshold concentrated below the median, or heterogeneous within the mid and upper feature_010 ranges. The new simple contrasts split the previously rejected median-to-third-quartile band at its midpoint, and split the upper quartile band at feature_010=1.0, to test whether the strong positive feature_021 association persists below the midpoint, disappears above the midpoint, and whether the extreme high tail differs from the lower-upper quartile band. For direction +1 simple mean_difference proposals, positive signed estimates mean feature_021=1 is associated with weaker outcome_006 dependency. For direction -1 interaction proposals, positive signed estimates mean raw attenuation or reversal in the named feature_010 subgroup relative to its complement in the same eligible population; anticipated_direction=-1 therefore encodes an expected raw negative interaction, i.e. attenuation. The outcome_006 operational 10 percent absolute-scale benchmark is approximately 0.0175. A new band claim would be considered meaningful only if the signed interval excludes the null and is materially beyond this benchmark while remaining coherent with adjacent bands. The feature_034 and feature_048 proposals ask whether the strong low-feature_010 effect is internally reproducible across an important binary predictor stratum and within the dominant feature_048 category, rather than being confined to one opaque subgroup. Alternative explanations include post hoc band instability, correlated predictors, small-cell chance, or weak associations that are not clinically meaningful. These comparisons remain dataset-specific associations only; no causal, mechanistic, or externally generalizable claim is intended.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative:
All estimates are already signed to the registered direction and were assessed without re-multiplication. For simple direction +1 outcome_006 contrasts, positive means feature_021=1 has a less negative score than feature_021=0, i.e. weaker dependency. For direction -1 interaction contrasts, positive signed estimates indicate raw attenuation or reversal of the feature_021 association in the named subgroup relative to its complement in the same eligible population. For outcome_006 I used an approximate 10 percent absolute-scale benchmark of about 0.0175 based on the observed absolute scale of the outcome. All requested cells exceeded the minimum 20-observation requirement.

Accepted dataset-specific localization: H323 (+0.403; lower +0.161), H324 (+0.557; lower +0.312), and H328 (+0.528; lower +0.328) show robust attenuation of the feature_021-outcome_006 association in the lower-mid, upper-mid, and extreme-high feature_010 bands relative to their complements. These effects are far above the clinical benchmark and have intervals excluding the null. H329 through H332 are accepted as internal reproducibility of the main low-feature_010 positive association: within feature_034=1, within feature_034=0, within feature_048=level_003, and within feature_048=level_003 at very low feature_010, the simple feature_021 contrasts are very large and tightly bounded positive (+0.799 to +0.821, all lower bounds >0.76). This supports the conclusion that the strongest feature_021 association is concentrated below the feature_010 median in this supplied dataset.

Rejected or unresolved mid/upper-band simple claims: H322 rejected because the upper-mid band estimate is negative and the interval crosses the null, providing no robust support for a meaningful positive association. H326 rejected because the extreme-high tail estimate is negative/near-null and the interval crosses the null, so a meaningful positive association is unsupported. H321, H325, and H327 remain unresolved: H321 has a positive point estimate above the benchmark but very wide uncertainty crossing the null; H325 has a high point but lower bound near zero, with small cells; H327 suggests attenuation but is too imprecise. These do not overturn the low-feature_010 localization, but they show that finer band estimates are unstable and should not be promoted.

Critical caveats remain: these are post hoc quantile bands in a dataset-specific discovery exercise with extensive multiplicity; opaque predictors may be correlated; latent confounding or assay-specific leakage cannot be excluded from labels alone. Thus accepted claims are robust internal associations and localization patterns, not causal effects, mechanistic claims, or externally generalizable results. Independent validation capacity is exhausted, so no validation request was made.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: No new validation or response deadlines are listed, and validation capacity is exhausted; therefore no assessments are submitted and no validation is requested. The accepted claim set remains unchanged and is interpreted strictly as dataset-specific associations. The strongest supported finding is feature_021 = 1 versus 0 for outcome_006. Because more negative scores mean stronger dependency, positive signed contrasts mean feature_021 = 1 is associated with weaker dependency. Discovery R121 gave +0.396 with 95 percent interval +0.325 to +0.467, and independent validation R127 gave +0.435 with adjusted interval +0.334 to +0.536. These effects are far above the 10 percent clinical benchmark and exclude the null. The association is localized to low feature_010: accepted large positive simple contrasts include H295, H298, H309, H329, H330, H331, and H332, and accepted attenuation interactions include H296, H301, H307, H308, H323, H324, and H328. Mid and upper simple bands are null, negative, or imprecise, including rejected H310, H322, and H326 and unresolved H321, H325, and H327; thus the best description is concentration below the feature_010 median, not a smooth gradient. Most other measured predictors and subgroups are not supported as meaningful effects. Validated negative or null lines include feature_002-outcome_006 after R53, feature_008-outcome_008 after R66, feature_043 interaction after R235, feature_057 interaction after R222, feature_048-outcome_009 subgroup effects after R209 and related validation, and feature_065-outcome_015 subgroup effect after R247. Unresolved evidence remains for raw feature_021-outcome_005, residual feature_065 associations with outcome_014 and outcome_015, some feature_048 subgroup contrasts, and many deferred comparisons. Because predictors are opaque, bands are post hoc, multiplicity is high, and no independent validation capacity remains, none of these findings should be treated as causal, mechanistic, or externally generalizable. The most informative next analysis is a pre-specified model-based robustness study of feature_021 and outcome_006, with covariate adjustment, non-linear or spline modeling of feature_010, formally tested interactions under multiplicity control, assay-level sensitivity, and confirmation in independent data.
